security_audit.summary: The repeated Ruby backtick detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not executable commands. The hardcoded URLs and gas-bidding snippets are instructional examples, but the skill contains dual-use MEV extraction guidance that could enable frontrunning, sandwiching, or hidden bidding. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: State allowed uses clearly, remove frontrunning and sandwich attack implementation cues, and focus examples on defensive analysis and user refund flows.
Reframe coinbase payment material as relay market risk, or remove instructions for hiding bids from competitors.
Mark Flashbots URLs as examples and require users to configure endpoints and keys outside skill text.

content.user_title: Stress Test DeFi and MEV Bots
content.value_statement: DeFi and MEV bots often fail when backtests ignore latency, gas, reorgs, and adversarial orderflow. This skill guides realistic simulation, risk controls, AMM math, and private bundle submission.
actual_capabilities: Explains arbitrage, gas, reorg, latency, and failure-rate adjustments for expected value calculations.
Provides architecture guidance for strategy engines, execution engines, risk engines, and kill switches.
Shows AMM price impact concepts for Uniswap V2, Uniswap V3, and Curve-style pools.
Outlines Foundry, Anvil, pending block, and bundle simulation workflows.
Summarizes MEV-Share, Flashbots bundles, private relay submission, and bundle inclusion handling.
Lists production checklists and common failure modes before launching trading automation.
limitations: It does not execute trades or verify live profitability.
Examples are educational and require legal, ethical, and protocol review.
Market conditions, relay APIs, and protocol behavior can change quickly.
It does not replace smart contract audits or financial risk review.

use_cases.title: Prelaunch Bot Review
use_cases.description: Check a DeFi bot design for stale state, failed transactions, gas auctions, and missing kill switches.

use_cases.title: Simulation Plan Design
use_cases.description: Create realistic fork, pending block, and bundle simulations before risking capital.

use_cases.title: MEV Risk Briefing
use_cases.description: Summarize how private orderflow, MEV-Share, and AMM mechanics affect execution risk.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bot Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: I am planning a DeFi arbitrage bot for [markets]. Identify the main risks, assumptions, and tests before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Realistic Backtests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate validation for a working prototype.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simulation plan for my bot. Include fork tests, pending state checks, gas uncertainty, bait detection, and failure-rate assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess MEV Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of orderflow and bundle submission.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this MEV execution plan. Compare public RPC, protected RPC, MEV-Share, and Flashbots bundles for risk and operational requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create Launch Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a launch readiness checklist for my DeFi bot. Include kill switches, capital limits, monitoring, reorg handling, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Review this arbitrage bot before mainnet launch.
output: Main risks: stale state, failed transactions, gas auction losses, bait opportunities, and missing capital limits.
Required tests: fork simulation, pending block simulation, bundle simulation, and one week of limited capital testing.
Launch decision: blocked until the kill switch and loss limits are implemented.

output_examples.input: Explain why my profitable backtest may fail live.
output_examples.output: The backtest likely uses confirmed historical state, known gas prices, and no mempool competition. Live execution needs latency, slippage, reorg, and failure assumptions.

output_examples.input: Compare public RPC and private bundle submission for my bot.
output_examples.output: Public RPC exposes pending transactions to competitors and can leak profitable intent. Private bundles reduce exposure but require simulation, bidding discipline, and inclusion handling.

best_practices: Simulate against pending or forked state before submitting real transactions.
Implement kill switches, capital limits, and alerting before strategy logic grows.
Calculate expected value after gas, failure rates, reorg risk, competition, and bait risk.
anti_patterns: Assuming arbitrage is risk-free because a historical backtest was profitable.
Sending profitable transactions through public RPC without considering mempool exposure.
Launching with real capital before failure handling, monitoring, and rollback paths exist.

faq.question: Does this skill trade or move funds?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples only. Users must build, test, and operate their own systems.

faq.question: Can it guarantee profitable MEV strategies?
faq.answer: No. It emphasizes why profitable backtests often fail under live gas, latency, and competition.

faq.question: Does it cover AMM math?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers price impact, slippage, Uniswap V2, Uniswap V3 ticks, fee tiers, and Curve-style risk.

faq.question: Does it include production risk controls?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers kill switches, loss limits, reorg handling, stale state checks, monitoring, and launch checklists.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: It can help beginners understand risks, but it assumes basic knowledge of DeFi, smart contracts, and trading systems.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
